title: The Real Architecture Behind GitHub Pages for Free Digital Product Store Hosting: The Honest Answer
author: COREMERCH
excerpt: Selling ebooks, courses, templates, fonts, and digital downloads with automated crypto delivery — no platform middleman, no payout delays, no geographic filter.

content.text: In Zimbabwe, where payment platforms like Stripe are severely restricted, selling digital products like ebooks, courses, and templates online requires a different approach. Traditional solutions like Gumroad and Payhip are not an option, and Stripe's absence has forced creators to think outside the box. That's where GitHub Pages comes in – a free hosting solution that can be used to create a digital product store, but only if you know the right architecture behind it.
What This Actually Is and Why It Matters

GitHub Pages is a static site generator that allows you to host your website for free on GitHub's servers. It's a great solution for digital product creators who want to sell their ebooks, courses, and templates without relying on payment platforms like Stripe. But what's important to note is that GitHub Pages is not a digital product store by itself – it's a hosting solution that requires additional infrastructure to turn it into a fully functional store.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

To turn GitHub Pages into a digital product store, you need to use a combination of other tools and services. For example, you'll need a backend logic solution like Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script to handle payment processing, order storage, and file delivery. You'll also need a database like Supabase or Google Sheets to store customer orders. And finally, you'll need a payment gateway like NOWPayments to enable automatic on-chain crypto payment verification.
Who This Is Built For and Why

The product types that work with automated crypto delivery are any digital files that can be stored and delivered via download link: ebooks in PDF or EPUB format, courses packaged as ZIP archives or delivered via hosted video links, Notion templates exported as files or share links, font families as ZIP archives of OTF and TTF files, Lightroom or Capture One preset packs, beat files as WAV or MP3 archives, plugin installers, stock photo packs, software license keys, and any other file-based product. The delivery system in Stack 01 uses Google Drive shared links. Stack 02 uses Cloudflare R2 presigned URLs with configurable expiry times — typically 24 to 72 hours — which prevents download links from being shared indefinitely after a single purchase. Both approaches work reliably and cost nothing beyond the storage used.
By using GitHub Pages as a hosting solution, you can maintain full control over your digital products and customer data.
The Components That Make It Work Together

The order management layer gives you complete visibility into every transaction your store processes. In Stack 01, every order is logged to a Google Sheet with the buyer's email, product purchased, payment amount in crypto and USD equivalent, transaction hash for on-chain verification, and delivery status. In Stack 02, orders are stored in a Supabase PostgreSQL database with the same fields plus additional metadata. Both can be exported as CSV at any time. The transaction hash provides cryptographic proof of every payment that does not depend on any platform's records — you can verify any transaction independently on a public blockchain explorer. This level of transparency and verifiability is structurally different from conventional payment processors, where transaction data is owned by the platform and subject to their record-keeping policies.
How to Use This Knowledge to Deploy Today

To deploy this architecture today, you'll need to start by setting up a GitHub Pages site and creating a Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script backend. Next, you'll need to set up a Supabase or Google Sheets database to store customer orders. Finally, you'll need to integrate NOWPayments into your store to enable automatic on-chain crypto payment verification. And that's it – you'll have a fully functional digital product store up and running in no time.
